metadata.title: A blackboard architecture for control
metadata.abstract_summary: A blackboard system solves a problem through independent knowledge sources that read and write a shared, structured workspace (the blackboard), coordinated by a separate control component that decides which knowledge source acts next - useful specifically when the right problem-solving strategy cannot be fixed in advance.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
sections.text: A blackboard system solves a problem through independent knowledge sources that read and write a shared, structured workspace (the blackboard), coordinated by a separate control component that decides which knowledge source acts next - useful specifically when the right problem-solving strategy cannot be fixed in advance.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A conceptual and architectural paper: defines the three generic components (knowledge sources, blackboard, control), then grounds the definition in the HEARSAY-II speech-understanding system and other implemented blackboard systems as worked examples of the architecture in practice.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Architectural description grounded in a real, implemented system (HEARSAY-II), not a purely theoretical proposal.
- Explicit that blackboard systems trade a clean, prescribed control flow for flexibility, and offers no formal guarantee about efficiency or termination - a cost later blackboard-system critiques focused on directly.
- Still the standard citation for the pattern itself, independent of whether a given modern system calls it a "blackboard" or something else (a shared event bus, a tuple space).
